[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Remove Covered Intervals** [LC 1288 · Remove Covered Intervals](https://leetcode.com/problems/remove-covered-intervals/){difficulty="Medium"}

The direct definition ("is there some other interval that contains this one?") is $O(n^2)$, fine for $n \le 1000$; the sort-based form is just as short and scales to $n = 10^5$ and beyond. The insight: **sort by start ascending, and for ties by end descending**. Once in that order, an interval $[a_i, b_i]$ is covered iff some earlier interval had the same or smaller start and a *larger or equal* end — which is equivalent to $b_i \le$ `max_end_so_far`. The tie-break matters: at equal start, sorting end descending puts the widest one first so any narrower same-start interval is correctly marked as covered; sorting end ascending would flag the widest as extending and miss the containment.

[Solved in full in @sec-int-p4-b.]{.card-link}
